arxiv-2305-02449.title: Bayesian Safety Validation for Failure Probability Estimation of Black-Box Systems
arxiv-2305-02449.creator: Robert J. Moss and Mykel J. Kochenderfer, Maxime Gariel and Arthur Dubois
arxiv-2305-02449.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Robert J. Moss and Mykel J. Kochenderfer, Maxime Gariel and Arthur Dubois. Estimating the probability of failure is an important step in the certification of safety-critical systems. Efficient estimation methods are often needed due to the challenges posed by high-dimensional input spaces, risky test scenarios, and computationally expensive simulators. This work frames the problem of black-box safety validation as a Bayesian optimization problem and introduces a method that iteratively fits a probabilistic surrogate model to efficiently predict failures.

arxiv-2312-15614.description: Abstract . Pre-trained models (PTMs) have achieved great success in various Software Engineering (SE) downstream tasks following the “pre-train then fine-tune” paradigm. pmc-11448185.creator: Ellen Casey, Tejal Sarika Patel, Joao Francisco Almeida, Jay Binder, Jonathan Bucke, Kenneth Duffy, Marcia Faustin, Yasunobu Iwasaki, David Kruse, Jason Laird, Torrance Laury, JF Mathieu, Josh Rigg, Chris Tomlinson, Cheryl Thomas, Keith A Stokes
pmc-11448185.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The incidence of injuries reported in artistic gymnastics varies greatly. This is partly due to inconsistencies in defining and reporting injuries in artistic gymnastics. The objective was to develop consistent definitions and methodology for reporting injuries in artistic gymnastics. A group of medical practitioners working with international-level artistic gymnasts from America, Asia, Australia and Europe came to a consensus on recommendations for defining and reporting injuries in artistic gymnastics.

pmc-11545758.title: Caregivers’ Mastery in Handling Gastrostomy at Home after Educational Intervention: Qualitative Descriptive Study
pmc-11545758.creator: Jeferson Moreira dos Santos, Larissa Chaves Pedreira, Roberta Pereira Góes, Maria Antônia Alves de Souza, Cristina Rosa Soares Lavareda Baixinho, Johis Ortega, Rosseirys Noelia De La Rosa, Anderson Reis Sousa, Valdenir Almeida da Silva, Ivana Santos Pinto, Jéssica Lane Pereira Santos, Letícia Chicha
pmc-11545758.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Effective hospital discharge planning is crucial, particularly in educating caregivers on handling medical devices. This education helps manage the patient’s signs and symptoms, prevents post-discharge complications, and reduces early readmissions. This study aimed to understand aspects involved in the acquisition of mastery by home caregivers, in handling care of a patient who just underwent gastrostomy, after educational intervention during hospitalization and telemonitoring upon return home. Methods: Qualitative descriptive study. It followed 15 caregivers of people with percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy.
